item.title: 350,000 families in Gaza Strip left homeless: ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
GAZA -- The Hamas-run Ministry of Public Works and Housing said Saturday that 350,000 families in the Gaza Strip were in urgent need of shelter amid widespread destruction of homes and infrastructure. In a press statement, the ministry said approximately 410,000 housing units had been damaged during the Israel-Hamas conflict, with 335,000 completely destroyed and another 75,000 uninhabitable. "It means that roughly 80 percent of buildings in the strip had been damaged," said the ministry, adding that approximately 90 percent of the enclave's infrastructure had been destroyed. It stressed that 350,000 families urgently needed shelter, including 270,000 families who had been living in tents for more than three years without the most basic necessities for a decent life. The ministry further warned that 7,500 families were at risk of flooding as the rainy season begins, with 2,500 of them requiring urgent relocation. The ministry estimated that approximately 200,000 worn-out tents needed to be replaced immediately before severe weather conditions intensify, urging the international community to establish a dedicated humanitarian corridor to deliver shelter supplies. It also called for the entry of heavy machinery, fuel and spare parts needed to clear rubble and reopen roads, as well as a permanent housing program based on a transparent database that safeguards residents' property rights.

item.title: China, Africa share poverty reduction approaches
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
ADDIS ABABA -- A high-level thematic forum was held on Saturday in Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital, to further deepen China-Africa cooperation on poverty reduction through enhanced exchanges of practical experience and development approaches. Held under the theme "China-Africa Exchange of Poverty Reduction Experience and Practical Approaches," the forum brought together representatives from China, Ethiopia, and other African countries to explore new avenues of cooperation and foster Sino-African institutional knowledge sharing in support of global poverty alleviation efforts. Experts and academicians at the forum called for translating shared development experience into practical, country-specific solutions while respecting each nation's independent path, noting that poverty is not destiny and can be overcome through targeted action, productive transformation, and sustained partnerships. Addressing the gathering, Xue Songyan, secretary-general of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS), noted that China has completed the largest poverty alleviation campaign in human history, realizing the United Nations poverty reduction goal 10 years ahead of schedule. Outlining five think tank priorities, Xue said CASS and the China-Africa Institute will advance academic exchanges, conduct joint field research, foster two-way communication on knowledge products, support talent cultivation through scholar exchanges, and strengthen linkages and cooperation with African think tanks. The forum emphasized greater alignment of Sino-African cooperation with national development strategies and local priorities, stressing that poverty reduction requires strong governance, institutional support, and active citizen participation. Tefera Derbew, former Ethiopian ambassador to China, noted that poverty is a multidimensional challenge affecting the dignity, stability, and potential of communities and nations. Ethiopia has pursued agricultural transformation, infrastructure expansion, human capital growth, environmental restoration, and economic reforms under its 10-year development plan and homegrown economic reform agenda to address structural constraints. Calling for enhanced cooperation across productive investments, technology transfer, and local capacity building, Derbew underscored the vital need to further deepen collaboration through country-specific programs aligned with national priorities that create jobs and help people permanently escape poverty. Participants stressed that poverty reduction should be integrated into broader economic and social development, combining infrastructure, agricultural improvement, education, and skills training to build long-term resilience rather than relying solely on temporary relief. For his part, Chinese Ambassador to Ethiopia Chen Hai described poverty as a common challenge facing humanity, and poverty reduction and development as issues bearing on the well-being of all humanity. As a large developing country, China has secured victory in the largest-scale poverty alleviation battle in human history, lifting nearly 100 million rural poor people out of poverty. China has eradicated absolute poverty across the board, fulfilling a millennium-old dream and century-long aspiration of the Chinese people, he said. Chen finally highlighted that China, pursuing the principles of sincerity, real results, amity, and good faith, stands ready to share poverty reduction concepts, experience, and approaches with partners in need, offering a useful reference for developing countries to independently explore their own paths to modernization, deliver mutual benefits and win-win outcomes, and inject new momentum into global poverty reduction efforts.

item.title: China claims women's 3,000m relay gold in Seoul
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
SEOUL -- China won the women's 3,000m relay at the Seoul stop of the 2026-2027 ISU Short Track World Tour on Saturday, claiming its first gold of the season on the circuit. Zhang Chutong put China in front at the start, and the team led through the first half of the race. Canada overtook China during a relay exchange but fell in the closing laps, allowing China to take the title in 4 minutes, 12.679 seconds. South Korea finished second, and the Individual Neutral Athletes (AIN2) team took third.

item.title: Why China-Russia-US summit hailed historic for world stability, peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
BEIJING -- World leaders and observers spoke highly of the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, saying the talks have brought the world hope for peace, stability and cooperation. Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the historic summit in the city of Shenzhen, South China, on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump. As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction. LANDMARK STEP FOR GLOBAL SECURITY At a White House news conference on Friday, Trump hailed the Shenzhen meeting as "one of the most momentous international summits in many years." He said the "historic summit" had produced a trilateral peace declaration in which China, Russia and the United States reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said China's efforts to host the summit will help create and open up space for meaningful dialogue and mutual understanding toward lasting peace and harmony. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said the three leaders had shown wisdom and statesmanship in taking a step that mattered to the wider international community. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said he noticed how often the leaders had spoken of peace during their meeting. At the United Nations, Farhan Haq, deputy spokesman for the secretary-general, said the organization welcomed efforts by world leaders, including those of the Security Council's permanent members, to seek common solutions to global problems. Denis Simon, former executive vice-chancellor of Duke Kunshan University, said the summit could open a new channel for dialogue on international security among the three countries whose decisions carry considerable military, economic and diplomatic weight. "I see the meeting as an important opening," said Paul Frimpong, executive director of the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. With several international crises unfolding at once, he said, sitting together gave each leader a chance to hear directly from the other two about the risks they considered most pressing and where they saw room to act together. Gergely Salat, a senior researcher at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, said the meeting showed that China has been maintaining channels with both Washington and Moscow and has enough credibility with both to bring them to the same table. "Few capitals could do that today," he said. FINDING RIGHT WAY TO GET ALONG At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. "China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said. Sourabh Gupta, a resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies in Washington, noted the repeated references at the summit to preserving the outcomes of World War II. As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries bear a special responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, he said. Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said advances in artificial intelligence were adding a new layer of risk for nuclear powers. Against that backdrop, he said, China's emphasis on preserving strategic stability at the summit sent an encouraging signal about the prospects for peace. Shraga Biran, head of Israel's Institute for Structural Reforms, pointed to the Middle East, noting that with several regional flashpoints in play, reliable communication can keep one miscalculation from triggering another and reduce the risk that a crisis escalates by accident. ENCOURAGING CONSENSUS Xi called on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world. Ezzat Saad, director of the Cairo-based Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said that a better understanding among the major countries could give diplomats more room to work and help contain tensions across the Middle East region. "When fuel and freight costs rise, businesses pay more to move goods, and families can feel it in food prices," said Frimpong with the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. In the heads of state declaration released following the summit, the three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. In regions recovering from conflict, Frimpong said, more reliable energy supplies would also make it easier for businesses to reopen and invest. For Alphonse Muleefu, principal of the College of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Rwanda, the declaration issued in Shenzhen showed that the three countries could find common ground. Building on it, he said, would take mutual respect, sustained dialogue and practical cooperation. "I believe this meeting marks an encouraging step toward a more stable world," he said.

item.title: Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle. Experts said Xi's speech at the gathering outlined China's vision for a stronger, more integrated Asia-Pacific community, offering a roadmap for the region to build on the achievements of the past three decades. They also said it could help deepen regional cooperation, create new opportunities for shared development and contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and beyond. A SHARED VISION In his Thursday speech, Xi stressed that building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. These requirements are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, said Herbert Sima, director of the China Studies Center at the University of Auckland, noting they not only provide guidance for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, but also offer valuable insights into addressing global uncertainties. Solidarity and mutual assistance form the foundation of cooperation, openness and connectivity provide a pathway for development, innovation and progress serve as the driving force for growth, while inclusive development is key to ensuring that cooperation is sustainable and benefits all parties, the expert explained. In his speech, Xi reviewed the achievements of the Asia-Pacific miracle over the past thirty-plus years, stressing the need to adapt to the new realities, take new strides and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the face of new opportunities and challenges. Xi's remarks have prompted experts to again reflect on the factors behind the region's remarkable economic growth and the prospects for its future development. Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of the Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the Asia-Pacific miracle had been driven by open cooperation, trade and investment, and the integration of regional industrial and supply chains. What Xi stressed about building the Asia-Pacific community offered a response to the challenges facing the region and a vision for future cooperation, he said. The expert particularly noted Xi's mention of "open regionalism" in his speech, saying that for developing economies such as Indonesia, the concept means access to broader markets and more convenient connectivity. Tran Thi Hai Yen, a researcher at the Institute for European and Americas Studies at Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi's vision comes at a timely moment, which addresses the four practical needs currently facing the Asia-Pacific region. As the rotating chair of APEC this year, she added, China has further clarified the direction of cooperation and underscored the urgency of accelerating joint efforts, helping translate long-term vision into concrete cooperation agendas. History proves that economies can prosper through trade with one another, and Xi reaffirmed the value of trade cooperation and open regionalism, said Craig Emerson, director of the Australia APEC Study Center. Such remarks are highly encouraging at a time when trade liberalization has faced growing skepticism in recent years, noted Emerson, a former Australian trade minister. "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon. "Economies in the Asia-Pacific region differ in terms of economic size, stages of development, history and culture, making the region highly diverse," he said. "This diversity should be regarded as a valuable resource. We should leverage our respective strengths, complement one another's weaknesses and turn these differences into new opportunities for cooperation." BUILDING PILLARS TOGETHER China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, Xi said in his speech. He also called for strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. On the importance of connectivity, Alvaro Echeverria, director of the Asia Pacific Chamber of Commerce in Chile, said the call to upgrade the pillar of connectivity was particularly relevant in the current international environment. Greater proximity helps create mutual understanding, Echeverria told Xinhua, saying he welcomes China's call to strengthen connectivity not only through physical infrastructure, but also through continued efforts to promote human development and closer people-to-people exchanges. These efforts could help rebuild trust at a time when the world faces considerable uncertainty and a lack of predictability, while the need for international coordination continues to grow, he added. Xi pointed out that China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, and announced that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation, and to establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support. In addition, Xi said that in line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, China will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific. China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs. "As a recognized technology leader in the digital economy, clean energy and related sectors, China can use these cooperation bodies to advance pragmatic cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies and build science and technology innovation partnerships," Mankevich said. Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development. "This approach of 'getting its own house in order first and then bringing partners along' demonstrates China's leading role and exemplary influence in regional cooperation," he said.

item.title: Intl network launched to streamline silk standards
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
The world's first international science and technology organization in the textile sector to be headquartered in China was formally established in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, on Friday, marking a new step in China-led international efforts to promote cooperation on silk industry standards, technology and development. With more than 100 member organizations from over 20 countries and regions, the agenda of the China-initiated International Network for Silk covers the entire silk value chain, including sericulture resource development, production and processing, and trade and investment, according to official information released during the founding ceremony. "Under the framework of the network, we should build a public service platform to share information, match supply and demand, enhance exchanges and advance cooperation, as well as to promote practical collaboration across the silk value chain," Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing said on Friday during the ceremony. Efforts should be made to strengthen mutual recognition of standards, align rules and promote industrial coordination in the silk sector, while building an integrated innovation ecosystem, he said. Zhang also called for greater cultural exchanges, including cross-border showcases of silk-making techniques, visits by inheritors of intangible cultural heritage and joint projects by designers from different countries. China's position as a major player in the global silk industry provides an important foundation for the initiative. The country accounted for about 75 percent of global cocoon production and more than 60 percent of raw silk exports by the end of 2025, according to the Ministry of Commerce.

item.title: Talks begin for economic partnership pact with Indonesia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto announced on Friday the start of negotiations to reach a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership agreement. During their meeting, Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on the two countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy and clean energy. He also called for efforts to actively build a blue partnership and reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. China is willing to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation and China-ASEAN, Xi said. Prabowo noted that he and Xi have met four times in recent years to push for significant progress in bilateral relations, and stressed that the strategic partnership between Indonesia and China is stronger than ever before. Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and recognizes Taiwan as a province of the People's Republic of China, Prabowo said. He thanked China for its longstanding support for Indonesia's economic and social development, adding that his country is willing to continuously deepen cooperation with China. He said Indonesia welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business, and vowed to provide a reliable, stable and predictable business environment.

item.title: Xi: Head-of-state diplomacy 'irreplaceable' for China-US ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping highlighted on Thursday the "irreplaceable" role of head-of-state diplomacy in guiding relations between China and the United States, urging concrete actions to sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in the relationship. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting. Both sides considered the meeting to be positive and constructive, according to a statement released after the meeting. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive relationship of strategic stability, implement the consensus reached by the two presidents, and build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, the statement said. This was the third meeting between Xi and Trump this year. The two presidents also met in Beijing in May, when Trump made a state visit to China, and in Washington in September, when Xi made a state visit to the US. Xi said that over the past few months, he and Trump have been working together to explore the right path for China and the US, the two major countries, to get along well with each other. The new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity has been well recognized by the peoples of both countries and welcomed by the international community, he said. Xi noted that the overall stability and positive momentum of China-US relations have brought tangible benefits to the people of the two countries, and injected stability and certainty into the world. He expressed his hope to continue working with Trump to jointly steer the giant ship of China-US relations in the right direction toward the future. Xi emphasized that building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented, groundbreaking endeavor that requires an enterprising spirit, hard and solid efforts, and the ability to get things done. To sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in China-US relations, the key is to take concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, he said, adding that communication between the working teams on both sides also needs to keep pace. Xi stressed that it is important to make a longer list of cooperation and a shorter list of problems. Differences that cannot be resolved for the time being should be managed in a constructive way to prevent them from escalating, he said. On the Taiwan question, Xi said the US should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-US relations. He called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns and work toward mutual benefit. Cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. He also underlined the need for China and the US to strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence and ensure that AI always remains under human control. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of US-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. Both sides should maintain the momentum of steady development of bilateral relations, and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence, and fairly address each other's concerns, Trump said. He told Xi that the US does not support "Taiwan independence". Trump congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability. The two presidents also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest. He Yadong, spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, announced on Thursday that the agricultural working group under the China-US Board of Trade will soon hold its first meeting. The two countries' economic and trade teams have maintained communication at various levels, and the two sides held the first meeting of the Board of Trade under the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Nov 13, the spokesman said at a regular news briefing in Beijing. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi calls for inclusive regional co-op based on solidarity, openness, innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
President Xi Jinping outlined economy and trade, connectivity, innovation and development as four pillars for building an Asia-Pacific community and opening up new prospects for regional cooperation, as he chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Thursday. The gathering marked the third time that China has hosted the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting, following those held in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. "Today, momentous changes not seen in a century are accelerating across the globe," Xi told the leaders and representatives of APEC economies and heads of international organizations attending the meeting. APEC's 21 member economies are home to more than one-third of the world's population and account for over 60 percent of global GDP. Xi called for efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship, he noted, adding that "to navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other". "We must expand our shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily build a shared sense of community," he said. He called for upholding openness and integration, advancing economic integration and championing free and open trade and investment. Development should benefit everyone, he said, while taking into account the different needs of Asia-Pacific economies. Xi said that China, an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, is ready to work with all parties to strengthen the pillar of economy and trade, upgrade the pillar of connectivity, foster the pillar of innovation and enhance the pillar of development. On trade, Xi said the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific is a shared vision of APEC members, and he called for steady progress in realizing this vision and setting a higher standard for openness. He urged efforts to align regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, reduce barriers to trade and investment, and help economies build the capacity to participate in high-standard economic and trade arrangements. Regarding connectivity, he called for stronger infrastructure networks, closer coordination of policies and regulations, and easier travel for business and tourism. Cultural and people-to-people exchanges should also be promoted to foster mutual understanding, he said. On innovation, Xi described the digital economy and artificial intelligence as engines of innovation-driven growth. "We should build an open ecosystem for innovation, encourage the broad application of AI, and promote the innovation-driven transformation and upgrading of industries," he said. On development, he emphasized the need to promote regional cooperation on energy and food security, deepen anti-corruption governance across borders, and expand green and low-carbon cooperation to achieve sustainable economic growth. He also called for improving livelihoods and investing in people to tap into the full potential of talent across the Asia-Pacific. "China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation," Xi said. He announced that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation, and will establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges. China will also set up cooperation institutions in areas including digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, he said. Leaders and representatives of member economies delivered remarks in turn. All parties spoke highly of the fruitful outcomes of the APEC China Year, thanked China for its excellent work, and made positive responses to the major initiatives and measures put forward by Xi. Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund, who was invited to brief the meeting on the state of the global economy, said that AI has had a material impact on global growth this year, helping counterbalance the economic effects of an energy supply shock. Describing AI as a significant factor in medium-term competitiveness, productivity and growth, she called on economies to develop digital infrastructure, prepare workers for the technology, and address risks to financial stability and cybersecurity. She also underscored the importance of dialogue and cooperation through forums such as APEC, saying that working together can help advance shared prosperity and peace. After listening to the other participants' remarks, Xi called for turning the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into action, maintaining a clear direction for cooperation and delivering solid results to continuously achieve tangible and accessible outcomes. At the conclusion of the meeting, leaders adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which puts forward the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, as well as three outcome documents covering trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnamese President To Lam, whose country will host APEC in 2027, welcomed leaders and representatives to attend next year's meeting. With China's leadership and the positive contributions of its members, APEC 2026 has achieved important accomplishments, adding momentum to economic integration and development in the Asia-Pacific, he said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn
